articles.title: Como Flávio compensou vantagem de Lula no Nordeste | G1
articles.standfirst: Senador superou presidente por quase 3,5 milhões de votos em SP e construiu bons saldos de votos nos estados da Região Sul.
articles.summary: Candidato do PL acumulou saldo de quase 3,5 milhões de votos em SP e também abriu boa vantagem nos estados do Sul.
articles.body:
A vantagem construída por Lula ( PT ) nos estados do Nordeste na votação deste domingo (4) não foi suficiente para superar o desempenho de Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ) em regiões de maior peso eleitoral.

Flávio terminou o 1º turno à frente, com 56,1 milhões de votos (47,03%) , contra 53,8 milhões de Lula (45,16%). A diferença foi de 2,2 milhões.

Com esses números, o filho superou a votação do pai, Jair Bolsonaro, que no 1º turno de 2022 conseguiu 51 milhões de votos, contra 57,2 milhões de Lula.

Os saldos de votos de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro

Em 2026, Lula registrou seus maiores saldos de votos no Nordeste, onde venceu em todos os estados e acumulou diferenças superiores a 3,2 milhões de votos na Bahia, 1,8 milhão em Pernambuco e 1,8 milhão no Ceará. Ao todo, Lula fez um saldo de 11 milhões de votos no Nordeste.

O resultado, porém, é contrabalançado pelos ganhos de Flávio Bolsonaro em estados de maior peso eleitoral. Considerando as demais regiões, o candidato do PL acumulou 13 milhões de votos a mais que Lula.

Gráfico mostra saldos de votos acumulados por Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula — Foto: Arte g1

O destaque é São Paulo, onde o senador abriu vantagem de 3,4 milhões de votos, o maior saldo. Também contribuíram para o desempenho os resultados no Rio de Janeiro, em Minas Gerais e no Espírito Santo.

Juntos, São Paulo, Minas Gerais e Rio de Janeiro somam mais de 40% dos eleitores do país.

Somente os saldos obtidos por Flávio em São Paulo e no Rio já tiraram boa parte da vantagem construída por Lula em estados nordestinos.

A força do senador na região foi complementada pelos resultados positivos no Sul, especialmente no Paraná e em Santa Catarina, onde as diferenças ultrapassaram 1,8 milhão de votos.

Assim, embora Lula tenha conseguido uma ampla dianteira no Nordeste, não foi suficiente para fazer com que o presidente terminasse à frente a votação deste domingo.

O peso eleitoral dos maiores colégios do Sudeste e a vantagem de Flávio em estados do Sul acabaram equilibrando a disputa nacional e garantiram ao senador um saldo superior na soma dos estados.

articles.summary: Levantamento parcial reúne 1.139 eleitos. Entre os 20 governadores incluídos, Lucas Ribeiro, de 37 anos, é o mais novo, e Jorginho Mello, de 70, o mais velho.
articles.body:
Alvinho Lira (PP-AL), filho de Arthur Lira — Foto: Reprodução

Alvinho Lira (PP-AL), de 20 anos, e Zé Teixeira (PL-MS), de 86, são o mais novo e o mais velho entre os 1.139 candidatos eleitos reunidos no levantamento parcial do g1 , com base nos dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) do primeiro turno das eleições de 2026.

Alvinho conquistou uma vaga de deputado federal por Alagoas. Já Zé Teixeira foi eleito deputado estadual por Mato Grosso do Sul.

Entre os mais jovens, Alvinho é seguido por Sandro Filho (PP-BA), de 21 anos, eleito deputado federal pela Bahia. Na sequência aparecem Poubel Filho (PL-RJ), Marcos Junior (Pode-TO) e Thiago Medina (PL-PE), todos com 23 anos.

Na outra ponta, Londres Machado (PP-MS), de 84 anos, aparece depois de Zé Teixeira. Os dois foram eleitos para a Assembleia Legislativa de Mato Grosso do Sul. Luiz Paulo (PSD-RJ) e José Esmeraldo (União-ES), ambos com 80 anos, vêm em seguida. Entre os 20 governadores eleitos em primeiro turno, Lucas Ribeiro (PP), na Paraíba, é o mais novo, com 37 anos. Jorginho Mello (PL), eleito em Santa Catarina, é o mais velho, com 70.

As idades foram calculadas a partir do nascimento informado ao TSE.

🔄 Esta reportagem está em atualização. O levantamento reúne os candidatos que já apareciam como eleitos nos arquivos consultados e ainda não representa o resultado completo do país. As posições podem mudar com a inclusão de novos resultados.

Lucas Ribeiro — Foto: Reprodução / TV Cabo Branco

Lucas Ribeiro (PP-PB), de 37 anos, e Jorginho Mello (PL-SC), de 70, estão nos extremos de idade entre os governadores classificados como eleitos nos arquivos consultados. A diferença entre as idades dos dois é de 33 anos.

Depois de Lucas, os mais novos são JHC (PSDB-AL), de 39 anos, e Dr. Daniel (Pode-PA), de 40. Entre os mais velhos, Jorginho é seguido por Otaviano Pivetta (Republicanos-MT), de 67 anos, e Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT-BA), de 61.

A atualização inclui Eduardo Braide (PSD-MA), de 50 anos, que passou a aparecer como eleito no arquivo de resultados do Maranhão.

Júlio César (PSD-PI), de 78, é o candidato ao senador mais velho eleito em 2026 — Foto: Reprodução

No Senado, Filipe Barros (PL-PR), de 35 anos, é o mais novo entre os eleitos incluídos no levantamento. Júlio César (PSD-PI), de 78, é o mais velho.

articles.title: Lula teve 1,7 milhão de votos a menos do que 2022 em SP, RJ e MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Estados concentram mais de 40% dos votos do eleitorado brasileiro. Senador ficou à frente do petista, e ambos disputam 2º turno em 25 de outubro.
articles.summary: Estados concentram mais de 40% dos votos do eleitorado brasileiro. Senador ficou à frente do petista, e ambos disputam 2º turno em 24 de outubro.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula — Foto: Evaristo Sá/AFP e Amanda Perobelli/Reuters

Os resultados das eleições de 2026 mostram que o presidente Lula (PT) perdeu cerca de 1,7 milhão de votos em São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro e Minas Gerais na comparação com o 1º turno da eleição presidencial de 2022.

Ao mesmo tempo, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) obteve 1,3 milhão de votos a mais nesses três estados do que seu pai, Jair Bolsonaro (PL), quatro anos antes.

1º turno em MG, RJ e SP — Foto: Infografia/g1

Juntos, São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro e Minas Gerais concentram mais de 40% do eleitorado brasileiro e contribuíram para a vantagem obtida pelo senador sobre o presidente. Em 2022, Lula havia ficado à frente de Jair Bolsonaro nesses mesmos estados. Os dois também disputaram o 2º turno naquele ano.

Veja, abaixo, a diferença de votações entre 2026 e 2022:

Diferença de votos no 1º turno da eleição presidencial em SP, RJ e MG de 2022 para 2026 — Foto: Arte/g1

Em uma eleição presidencial marcada pela consolidação da polarização entre bolsonarismo e petismo, o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) vão disputar o segundo turno das eleições presidenciais no próximo dia 25 de outubro.

A confirmação de que haverá segundo turno foi anunciada pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) neste domingo (4), às 20h56, quando 96,78% das urnas já tinham sido apuradas. Àquela altura, Flávio Bolsonaro tinha 47,39% dos votos, e Lula, tinha 44,74%.

A diferença entre Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Lula (PT) é a menor já registrada em um primeiro turno de eleição presidencial desde a redemocratização. Em número de votos, a diferença entre os dois foi de cerca de 2,4 milhões. Como nenhum candidato alcançou mais da metade dos votos válidos, Flávio e Lula disputarão o segundo turno, marcado para 25 de outubro.

Em 2022, Lula obteve 48,43% dos votos válidos e Jair Bolsonaro (PL), 43,2%, uma distância de 5,23 pontos percentuais. Até então, essa tinha sido a menor diferença de pontuação na disputa.

Daqui a três semanas, os eleitores voltam às urnas para definir se Flávio Bolsonaro governará o país pelos próximos quatro anos ou se Lula terá um quarto mandato presidencial.

O senador liderou no Distrito Federal e em 14 estados neste primeiro turno — todas as unidades federativas das regiões Sul, Sudeste e Centro-Oeste.

Já o atual presidente teve mais votos em 12 estados — todos da região Nordeste e alguns da região Norte.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro reúne campanha nesta segunda para traçar estratégia para o segundo turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Previsão é que Flávio se reúna com o governador reeleito de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), durante a tarde.
articles.summary: Previsão é que Flávio se reúna com o governador reeleito de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), durante a tarde.
articles.body:
O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), candidato à Presidência da República, iniciou a manhã desta segunda-feira (5) reunido com integrantes de sua equipe de campanha para discutir os próximos passos da disputa no segundo turno contra o atual presidente, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

Em uma eleição presidencial marcada pela consolidação da polarização entre bolsonarismo e petismo, Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula vão disputar o segundo turno das eleições presidenciais no próximo dia 25 de outubro.

Com todas as urnas apuradas, o resultado divulgado pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) mostra Flávio Bolsonaro à frente, com 47,03% dos votos, e Lula em segundo lugar, com 45,16%.

Para o candidato do PL, as primeiras horas do dia serão dedicadas a reuniões internas de planejamento da campanha.

Flávio Bolsonaro fala após ida ao 2º turno — Foto: EVARISTO SA/AFP

Também há previsão de um encontro de Flávio com o governador reeleito de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos). A reunião ainda não tem horário definido, mas deve ocorrer durante a tarde.

O encontro foi anunciado pelo próprio Tarcísio no domingo (4) e, segundo integrantes da campanha de Flávio, a possibilidade também foi comunicada à equipe do candidato.

Daqui a três semanas, os eleitores voltam às urnas para definir se Flávio Bolsonaro governará o país pelos próximos quatro anos ou se Lula terá um quarto mandato presidencial.

Se Flávio for eleito, tomará posse, aos 45 anos, no dia 5 de janeiro de 2027, na cadeira ocupada por seu pai, Jair Bolsonaro, entre 2019 e 2022.

Se vencer, Lula assumirá o quarto mandato aos 81 anos e será o primeiro brasileiro a presidir o país quatro vezes.

Flávio e Lula deixaram para trás Augusto Cury (Avante), Renan Santos (Missão), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Romeu Zema (Novo), Edmilson Dias (PCB), Hertz Dias (PSTU), Samara Martins (UP), Wilson Grassi (Democrata), Clariana Barão (DC) e Rui Costa Pimenta (PCO).

articles.title: Com 108 mulheres eleitas, Câmara dos Deputados terá maior bancada feminina da história | G1
articles.standfirst: Pela Lei das Eleições, pelo menos 30% dos candidatos devem ser de um gênero e, consequentemente, no máximo 70% podem ser do outro.
articles.summary: Pela Lei das Eleições, pelo menos 30% dos candidatos devem ser de um gênero e, consequentemente, no máximo 70% podem ser do outro.
articles.body:
A Câmara dos Deputados terá, a partir de 2027, a maior bancada feminina de sua história.

Nesse domingo (4) foram 108 mulheres eleitas, um aumento de 17 cadeiras em comparação as eleições de 2022, quando 91 deputadas federais conquistaram uma vaga.

Entre os partidos que mais elegeram mulheres em 2026 estão PT, com 26, e PL, com 22 .

A votação deste domingo confirma uma crescente da bancada feminina nas últimas três eleições.

Nas eleições proporcionais — para deputado federal, deputado estadual, deputado distrital e vereador —, os partidos e federações precisam respeitar uma cota mínima de candidaturas de cada gênero.

Pela Lei das Eleições, pelo menos 30% dos candidatos devem ser de um gênero e, consequentemente, no máximo 70% podem ser do outro.

Na prática, como os homens são maioria entre os candidatos, a regra funciona principalmente como uma garantia de que ao menos 30% das candidaturas sejam de mulheres.

A legislação também garante recursos para essas candidaturas. As mulheres devem receber pelo menos 30% dos recursos públicos destinados às campanhas e do tempo de propaganda eleitoral gratuita.

Se elas representarem mais de 30% das candidaturas, a parcela de recursos deve aumentar na mesma proporção. A regra, porém, não estabelece um número mínimo de mulheres que precisam ser eleitas, mas apenas condições mínimas para a participação feminina na disputa.

Representação de pretos, pardos e indígenas

A eleição deste domingo manteve em 135 cadeiras o número de deputados pretos e pardos .

O PL elegeu 81 deputados federais e consolidou-se como a maior bancada no Congresso nas eleições de 2026. O PT, em segundo lugar, ficou com 47.

articles.summary: Na eleição Senado 2026, MDB e partidos do Centrão elegeram 17 nomes, mas o peso proporcional do grupo caiu em relação ao pleito de 2022.
articles.body:
Plenário do Senado Federal — Foto: Jonas Pereira/Agência Senado

Na disputa pelo Senado, o MDB, o União Brasil, o Progressistas, o Republicanos e o PSD elegeram, juntos, 17 parlamentares. Somados, esses partidos, que integram o bloco do chamado Centrão, conquistaram quatro cadeiras a mais que na eleição anterior.

Mas, proporcionalmente, houve queda uma queda de desempenho. Entenda por quê:

2022 - havia 27 vagas em jogo, das quais 13 (ou 48%) ficaram com MDB, União Brasil, Progressistas, Republicanos e PSD.

2026 - havia 54 vagas em jogo, das quais 17 (ou 31%) ficaram com MDB, União Brasil, Progressistas, Republicanos e PSD.

Considerando todas as siglas, o PL teve o maior número de senadores eleitos em 2026, conquistando 19 cadeiras. Com o resultado, o partido salta para 28 representantes e terá a maior bancada do Senado .

articles.title: Veja partidos que ficaram abaixo da cláusula de barreira | G1
articles.standfirst: Regra exige votação mínima ou número de deputados eleitos, com presença em pelo menos nove estados ou no DF. Decisões judiciais e reorganizações partidárias ainda podem alterar o acesso ao Fundo Partidário e à propaganda no rádio e na TV.
articles.summary: Regra exige votação mínima ou número de deputados eleitos, com presença em pelo menos nove estados ou no DF.
articles.body:
A federação PSOL/Rede, o PDT, o Avante, o Missão e a federação Renovação Solidária, formada por PRD e Solidariedade, ficaram abaixo dos requisitos da cláusula de barreira na eleição 2026. É o que mostram dados da apuração do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) consultados na madrugada desta segunda-feira (5).

As cinco agremiações aparecem com cadeiras na distribuição de vagas para a Câmara dos Deputados. Mesmo assim, não alcançam a combinação de votos ou de deputados com a presença mínima pelo país exigida pela regra.

A cláusula de barreira, também chamada de cláusula de desempenho, condiciona o acesso ao Fundo Partidário e ao tempo gratuito de propaganda no rádio e na TV. Ficar abaixo dela não impede a posse dos deputados eleitos nem provoca o fechamento do partido.

O PSOL/Rede ultrapassou o percentual nacional necessário, mas atingiu o mínimo estadual em apenas oito unidades da Federação. No Espírito Santo, ficou a 185 votos do patamar calculado sobre o total de votos válidos apurado.

O cenário ainda pode mudar com decisões judiciais que alterem a validade dos votos e levem a uma nova totalização. Fusões e incorporações de partidos também podem modificar o cumprimento da cláusula. Essas possibilidades, porém, não representam uma reversão garantida.

Para superar a cláusula nesta eleição, cada partido ou federação precisa cumprir pelo menos um de dois critérios:

Pela votação : obter ao menos 2,5% dos votos válidos nacionais para deputado federal e alcançar pelo menos 1,5% dos votos válidos em cada uma de, no mínimo, nove unidades da Federação.

Pelas cadeiras : eleger ao menos 13 deputados federais, distribuídos por pelo menos nove unidades da Federação.

O Distrito Federal entra nessa contagem. No caso das federações, os resultados dos partidos integrantes são considerados em conjunto.

Isso significa que uma votação expressiva concentrada em poucos estados pode não ser suficiente. Da mesma forma, eleger mais de 13 deputados não garante o cumprimento da regra se eles vierem de menos de nove unidades da Federação.

Entre as agremiações com cadeiras na distribuição de vagas consultada, o cenário é o seguinte:

A federação tem 4,89% dos votos válidos nacionais, acima dos 2,5% exigidos. O obstáculo é a distribuição pelo país.

Onde alcançou pelo menos 1,5% dos votos: Ceará, Distrito Federal, Minas Gerais, Pará, Pernambuco, Rio de Janeiro, Rio Grande do Sul e São Paulo. São oito unidades da Federação.

Onde aparecem suas 15 cadeiras: São Paulo, com seis; Rio de Janeiro, com quatro; Minas Gerais, com duas; Distrito Federal, Pernambuco e Rio Grande do Sul, com uma cada.

Assim, a federação também não cumpre o segundo critério: ultrapassa o mínimo de 13 deputados, mas suas vagas estão concentradas em seis unidades da Federação, quando seriam necessárias nove.

A federação tem 1,86% dos votos válidos nacionais, abaixo dos 2,5% exigidos.

Onde alcançou pelo menos 1,5% dos votos: Ceará, Goiás, Maranhão, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Rondônia e São Paulo. São sete estados.

Onde aparecem suas sete cadeiras: Ceará, com duas; Goiás, Maranhão, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro e São Paulo, com uma cada.

A federação não alcança o percentual nacional nem a presença mínima em nove unidades da Federação. Também fica abaixo dos 13 deputados necessários pelo critério de cadeiras.

O partido tem 1,64% dos votos válidos nacionais, abaixo do mínimo exigido.

Onde alcançou pelo menos 1,5% dos votos: Amapá, Bahia, Ceará, Maranhão, Paraná, Rio de Janeiro, Rio Grande do Sul e Roraima. São oito estados.

Onde aparecem suas seis cadeiras: Amapá, com duas; Bahia, Maranhão, Rio de Janeiro e Rio Grande do Sul, com uma cada.

O PDT fica abaixo dos dois critérios: não chega aos 2,5% nacionais nem ao mínimo estadual em nove unidades da Federação e aparece com menos de 13 deputados, distribuídos por cinco estados.

O partido tem 1,59% dos votos válidos nacionais, também abaixo dos 2,5%.

Onde alcançou pelo menos 1,5% dos votos: Amazonas, Bahia, Maranhão, Minas Gerais, Pernambuco e Rio de Janeiro. São seis estados.

Onde aparecem suas cinco cadeiras: Bahia, com três; Minas Gerais e Pernambuco, com uma cada.

Além de não alcançar o percentual nacional, o Avante fica abaixo da distribuição geográfica exigida e do número mínimo de deputados.

O partido tem 1,08% dos votos válidos nacionais.

Onde alcançou pelo menos 1,5% dos votos: somente em São Paulo.

Onde aparece sua cadeira: São Paulo, com uma vaga.

O Missão, portanto, não alcança nenhum dos dois critérios.

Também estão abaixo dos requisitos, sem cadeiras na distribuição consultada, DC, UP, Mobiliza, Democrata, PSTU, Agir e PCO.

Os números de cadeiras correspondem à distribuição informada nos arquivos do TSE. Em parte dos estados, a marcação individual dos candidatos eleitos ainda não estava concluída.

O Espírito Santo poderia ser a nona unidade da Federação em que o PSOL/Rede alcançaria pelo menos 1,5% dos votos válidos para deputado federal.

Com todas as seções totalizadas, o resultado no estado foi:

Total de votos válidos para deputado federal: 2.134.985.

Votos do PSOL/Rede, somando candidatos e legenda: 31.839.

Quantidade mínima para alcançar 1,5% desse total: 32.024 votos.

A federação ficou com aproximadamente 1,49% da votação válida no estado. A distância de 185 votos considera o total de votos válidos já apurado: uma eventual mudança nesse total exige refazer a conta.

Uma das possibilidades é uma decisão judicial que altere quais votos são considerados válidos. Quando uma mudança na situação jurídica de candidaturas, partidos ou federações afeta o resultado, a Justiça Eleitoral deve realizar uma nova totalização. Isso pode modificar os percentuais e a distribuição de vagas.

No caso do PSOL/Rede, a anulação de votos de outras legendas no Espírito Santo poderia reduzir o total usado como base para calcular os 1,5%. Assim, a participação da federação aumentaria mesmo sem o acréscimo de votos a seu favor.

Outra possibilidade é a validação de votos que hoje não integram a votação válida, caso decisões sobre candidaturas sejam revertidas. O efeito dependeria da quantidade de votos e do estado, com novo cálculo dos percentuais.

Também há o caminho da reorganização partidária. Fusões e incorporações podem permitir a soma dos resultados das legendas envolvidas. Foi o que aconteceu com o Solidariedade após incorporar o Pros: em 2023, o TSE reconheceu que a legenda passou a ter direito ao Fundo Partidário e à propaganda partidária gratuita.

O que acontece com os partidos e os eleitos

Não superar a cláusula não cancela o registro do partido nem retira os mandatos conquistados. Os parlamentares eleitos podem permanecer na legenda.

O TSE também reconhece a possibilidade de vereadores e deputados estaduais e federais migrarem, sem perda do mandato, de um partido que não atingiu a cláusula para outro que tenha cumprido os requisitos, a partir da proclamação dos eleitos.

A restrição financeira diz respeito ao Fundo Partidário, usado no custeio das atividades das legendas. Ele é diferente do Fundo Eleitoral, destinado ao financiamento das campanhas. Segundo a jurisprudência do TSE, não alcançar a cláusula não impede, por si só, o acesso ao Fundo Eleitoral.

Os cálculos consideram os arquivos oficiais de resultados para deputado federal das 27 unidades da Federação. Foram somados os votos válidos dados aos candidatos e às legendas, com os partidos federados agrupados. Também foram verificadas as cadeiras informadas pelo TSE e sua distribuição pelo país.

Na consulta, os arquivos ainda indicavam uma seção pendente no Amazonas e seis no Maranhão. Minas Gerais e São Paulo já tinham todas as seções totalizadas, mas ainda não apareciam com a totalização final concluída. O PCB não constava nos arquivos de deputado federal consultados e, por isso, não recebeu um total de votos neste cálculo.

O quadro retrata a apuração disponível e não equivale a uma relação definitiva homologada pelo TSE dos partidos que terão acesso aos recursos e à propaganda na próxima legislatura.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro conta com Tarcísio em SP e avanço no Nordeste para vencer no segundo turno | G1
articles.body:
A posição em primeiro lugar de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no primeiro turno, classificada de uma demonstração de força da direita, vai garantir apoios expressivos no segundo turno para chegar à Presidência da República.

Se havia alguma dúvida sobre a disposição do governador reeleito de São Paulo, Tarcísio Gomes de Freitas (Republicanos), de entrar de "corpo e alma" na fase final, agora, na campanha bolsonarista, já não há mais.

O apoio de Tarcísio de Freitas é considerado fundamental para que Flávio Bolsonaro amplie sua vitória no Sudeste.

"A participação do Tarcísio na reta final do primeiro turno foi fundamental. Os petistas contavam que ele iria fazer corpo mole, mas não fez", avalia um aliado do filho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro.

Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) durante a Festa do Peão de Barreto — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

A equipe de Flávio Bolsonaro vai traçar ainda uma estratégia para reduzir a diferença para Lula no Nordeste.

No primeiro turno, o petista teve menos voto neste ano do que em 2022. Perdeu quase 3% dos votos na comparação com a última eleição, cerca de 258 mil na região nordestina.

Em todo país, Lula perdeu quase 3,4 milhões de votos, enquanto Flávio Bolsonaro conquistou cerca de 5 milhões a mais do que seu pai em 2022.

"Vamos crescer ainda mais no Sudeste e Sul e conquistar mais votos no Nordeste. Essa será nossa estratégia. Teremos mais apoios em todo país do que o presidente Lula, estamos confiantes de que vamos ganhar a eleição no segundo turno", disse o coordenador da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro, o senador Rogério Marino (PL-RN).

articles.title: Don’t fear the digital price tag
articles.summary: Just as the notion of manually counting sales and inventory seems antiquated for supermarkets today, the time will come when paper price tags and shelf stickers will seem outdated and unnecessarily costly and wasteful.
articles.body:
A half century ago, consumer groups fought the use of bar code scanners in grocery stores over concerns that they would make it easier to rip people off and charge higher prices. There was even a concern that the laser would burn people .

Today, retailers around the world are adopting electronic shelf labels , also known as electronic shelf tags, in stores. They replace printed shelf tags and allow for prices to be set and adjusted using computers or tablets.

About 80 percent of supermarkets in Europe are using electronic labels, but adoption has been slower in the U.S., due to political opposition over concerns about price gouging and other predatory practices. A recent report by the AFL-CIO, the largest federation of labor unions in the country, echoed concerns about higher grocery prices and lost jobs and wages due to electronic label adoption.

Technological adoption has been a driving force of change in the grocery industry for more than a century. Labor-saving innovations, from shopping carts to bar code scanners to self-checkouts, have transformed the supermarket experience and proven to be beneficial for both consumers and operators. We can scarcely imagine a supermarket today without these amenities.

And importantly, despite these innovations, jobs in the grocery sector have not disappeared. For example, California is home to the largest food retailing sector in the country, and statewide grocery employment has increased by 38 percent since 1992, outpacing the state’s population, which has grown 28 percent over the same time.

Electronic shelf labels are unlikely to eliminate jobs in the grocery sector; despite growth in employment, labor remains a challenge for supermarkets. Food retailing has one of the highest turnover rates among all major industries in the country, reflecting challenges with retention and job satisfaction. And industry surveys repeatedly show that labor recruitment and retention are among the largest challenges and concerns facing supermarket operators. By eliminating the task of replacing shelf labels, workers have more time to work registers, bag groceries, stock shelves, assist shoppers and keep the store clean. Overall, store-wide productivity can increase with electronic label adoption as labor is reallocated and used more effectively.

Electronic shelf labels are not likely to lead to price increases or unfair pricing practices, either — in fact, they may result in lower and more efficient prices.

Research has long shown that food prices are notoriously sticky , meaning they do not change even when costs like energy or commodity prices suggest they should. Sticky prices are inefficient and result in problems for both retailers and consumers, including foregone profits and food waste. One of the factors behind sticky, stubborn prices is menu costs — literally the cost of changing prices in the store. A typical supermarket carries around 40,000 products; changing even a small share of them requires substantial labor and printing costs. Supermarkets using electronic labels can adjust prices more easily, allowing operators to revert prices to their previous and accurate levels as cost pressures ease.

Concerns about surveillance pricing, price gouging and other predatory tactics are distinct from the adoption of electronic labels in supermarkets. Regulation can and should address these concerns to ensure that the pursuit of profits doesn’t get in the way of food security. Electronic shelf labels have been prominent in Europe for years and there is no evidence that food prices have increased as a result. Surveillance pricing can be prevented with laws that prevent practices such as customer facial scans or other identifying steps during the shopping experience. Most states already have price gouging laws in effect that define the act and establish penalties, and these laws will remain in place for both printed and digital prices.

The U.S. grocery industry remains highly competitive, and most supermarkets operate on very thin margins . Electronic shelf labels and other technologies that reduce operating costs provide a path toward stabilizing and reducing food price inflation.

We need to provide tools for supermarkets and other retailers to manage their stores efficiently and set prices accurately, while keeping regulatory guardrails in place to prevent anticompetitive pricing behavior among bad actors. The story of bar code scanners is poised to play out again. Just as the notion of manually counting sales and inventory seems antiquated for supermarkets today, the time will come when paper price tags and shelf stickers will seem outdated and unnecessarily costly and wasteful.

Richard Volpe is professor of agribusiness at California Polytechnic State University at San Luis Obispo.

articles.title: Maher predicts GOP will get ‘historical a‑‑ whooping’ in midterms
articles.summary: Bill Maher says Republicans should be prepared to receive a “historical a‑‑ whooping” in the midterm elections. “They’re going to get their a‑‑ kicked. articles.body:
Bill Maher says Republicans should be prepared to receive a “historical a‑‑ whooping” in the midterm elections.

“They’re going to get their a‑‑ kicked. It’s going to be brutal,” Maher said of the GOP in a Sunday interview with Fareed Zakaria on CNN’s “GPS.”

“He’s lost even a lot of his own people,” the HBO “Real Time” host said, describing polls indicating waning support for President Trump.

“Trump screwed the pooch. That’s what happened. He got drunk with power,” Maher said.

“This is the pattern in this country: Somebody gets elected, they go way too far with their side of things. Biden did it to a degree with wokeness, and he was too feeble to fight the far-left,” Maher said of the former president.

“It was so easy just to come in and undo the bad, but nobody does that,” the 70-year-old comedian continued.

“It’s going to be a classic, historical a‑‑ whooping,” Maher said of Republicans’ chances in the midterm elections.

“Now, 2028 is a different story,” he added.

“The Democrats have a crazy animal living in their house called the DSA, and they believe truly insane things, and they’re the energy of the party,” Maher said of the growing influence of the Democratic Socialists of America.

“And they’re going to make ‘Gaza is a genocide’ a litmus test, and a lot of other really stupid stuff,” he added.

“But this electorate right now is saying, ‘We will get to that issue. Right now, we have one piece of business in front of us, and that is to let Donald Trump know we don’t like what he did. He went too far,'” Maher said.

“This is what we need to register our feelings on in 2026. We’ll get to the other stuff later, perhaps. But right now, we have one message: Donald Trump went too far, and his party will pay,” Maher said.

But Democrats, Maher said, may “misinterpret” their expected gains in the midterm elections.

“They will misinterpret the thumping that the Republicans get as an endorsement for the insanity that a good part of the party wants to march toward, and I’m talking about DSA ideas about like abolishing the police,” Maher said.

articles.title: Senate GOP PAC set to invest $14M in tight Kansas Senate race
articles.summary: The Senate Leadership Fund (SLF), a PAC aligned with Republican Senate leadership, is upping its spending in Kansas as the race for Senate heats up. articles.body:
The Senate Leadership Fund (SLF), a PAC aligned with Republican Senate leadership, is upping its spending in Kansas as the race for Senate heats up.

The group plans to invest $14 million to support incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall (R-Kan.), according to a source familiar with the SLF’s plans. Much of that will go toward ads attacking the Democratic candidate, Adam Hamilton, a political newcomer and pastor who founded the largest United Methodist church in the country. This spending was first reported by Punchbowl .

Kansas is not usually a competitive opportunity for Senate Democrats, as a Democrat has not won a Senate seat there in nearly a century. But Hamilton’s profile paired with low approval ratings for the GOP and President Trump nationally are weighing down Republicans’ chances in even the reddest of states.

Last week, the SLF pivoted some money from North Carolina, where Democrat Roy Cooper leads the GOP’s Michael Whatley in polling for the race to succeed retiring Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), to Kansas.

Cook Political Report and Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ) both rate the Kansas Senate race as lean Republican — one notch away from the toss-up column. Cook rates North Carolina as leaning in Democrats’ favor, while DDHQ says the party is likely to clinch the open seat.

articles.title: Repealing the roadless rule ignores public approval
articles.summary: New Mexico Sen. Martin Heinrich urged the public to voice their opposition to the administration’s efforts to repeal the roadless rule, which protects critical habitats and recreational areas from development.
articles.body:
For most Americans, September marks the end of summer and the beginning of the school year. But for hunters like me, it also marks the beginning of elk season — the few months that we rely on each year to help fill our freezers.

As an avid sportsman and conservationist, I have been harvesting wild game for decades. When I am scouting my hunt, I look for the places where people aren’t. Elk and other wildlife need food, water and security cover — none of which exist near roads.

That is one reason the Forest Service created the roadless rule: to preserve some of our last remaining stretches of national forest from development. These areas are vital not just for hunters and anglers but also for wildlife habitat, clean drinking water and outdoor recreation. Yet the Trump administration is working to repeal the roadless rule without giving the public a real opportunity to weigh in on the issue. That should concern everyone who cares about our public lands.

Our public lands are the physical manifestation of Jeffersonian democracy: The widespread ownership of public lands, managed by and distributed for all, giving each of us a say over the very land that makes up our country. And nowhere is that clearer than at a public comment meeting on a government public lands proposal.

I’ve been to these meetings. I sat in a packed public hearing room in New Mexico when the roadless rule was just a proposal and listened to the public comment. Back then, 95 percent of people agreed with the roadless rule. By last year, that number had grown to 99 percent .

The bottom line is this: The roadless rule is overwhelmingly popular, including with sportsmen, anglers, campers and recreators. It is so popular that the administration knows it will lose if it consults the public on dismantling it. Thus, the administration is simply refusing to hold public meetings at all. That is not only insulting — it is undemocratic. And it is a failure to listen to the people these lands belong to.

Now, the administration will try to tell you that repealing the roadless rule is for your own good. I am here to say that it is not telling you the truth.

The administration will tell you that repealing the roadless rule will reduce wildfires. The evidence tells a completely different story. A recent study found that 80 percent of human-caused fires happen within a half mile of a road. Roadless areas thus reduce fire risk rather than increasing it.

The administration will tell you that repealing the roadless rule will create the roads we need to improve our economy. The truth is, we have enough roads. The U.S. Forest Service has 371,000 miles of roads already — roughly eight times more than the entire U.S. interstate highway system. And the maintenance backlog for these forest roads is $6.1 billion. When you are in a hole that deep, the first thing to do is to stop digging.

Less than 5 percent of the U.S. is roadless or wilderness. Meanwhile, the recreation economy — which often relies on roadless areas and public lands — represents a whopping $1.3 trillion in economic output, almost 2.4 percent of the entire U.S. GDP . And hunting generates $33.5 billion in wages and income, with a total economic output of over $107 billion . That is greater than the GDP of 121 countries.

Our public lands are already driving enormous economic activity. We should be asking how to preserve these places — not how to put more roads through them.

As someone who has been fighting this fight in Congress for years, I also know this fight is about more than the roadless rule.

Last July, when the administration threatened to sell off half of our public lands, the uproar was so loud that they had to turn tail and run. Now we’re seeing another attempt to chip away at public lands protections that keep our public lands in public hands — this time by repealing the roadless rule and limiting the public’s ability to make their voices heard.

These roadless areas are some of our most special places. From the trout-filled headwaters of the Pecos River, to the bighorn habitat of the Bootheel, to the junipers and ponderosa pine forests of the Carson National Forest: New Mexico’s identity is in roadless areas.

Roadless areas are the backcountry places where we hunt, fish and pass our traditions on to the next generation. That’s why this fight matters.

For an administration that talks a big game, they are awfully afraid to go out to the people and places their decisions impact — because they know there will be opposition. I often say that our public lands are the anvil on which our American identity has been forged. Without the roadless rule, many of those places won’t survive.

So, to the administration, I have a simple request: Hold public meetings. Listen to the people who hunt, fish and recreate in these areas. Let them have a real say before you make a decision that could permanently change some of our most treasured lands.

And to the public: Make your voices heard. Our public lands are ours — and I urge you to speak up to keep it that way.

To submit a comment to the Forest Service, you can use this website until Oct. 6.

Martin Heinrich is the senior U.S. senator from New Mexico and the ranking Democratic member of the Energy and Natural Resources Committee. He is an avid sportsman and a lifelong conservationist.

articles.title: Latino voters favor Democratic control of Congress by 24-point margin: Survey
articles.summary: Latino voters prefer Democrats take control of Congress after the midterms and their opinions of President Trump’s performance remain poor, according to a new poll by NBC News and Telemundo. While the Latino vote was key to Trump’s win in 2024 as many Latino voters swung to the right, that trend may be reversing. Among…
articles.body:
Latino voters prefer Democrats take control of Congress after the midterms and their opinions of President Trump’s performance remain poor, according to a new poll by NBC News and Telemundo.

While the Latino vote was key to Trump’s win in 2024 as many Latino voters swung to the right, that trend may be reversing . Among the 800 registered Latino voters surveyed in September, 69 percent disapproved of Trump’s performance as president while 59 percent preferred that Democrats win the November elections. Just 35 percent said they wanted the GOP to clinch control of Congress.

The poll showed a growing negative sentiment for the GOP among Latinos — who make up about 16 percent of the total electorate — with 62 percent of respondents reporting a negative view of the party compared with 46 percent in September 2024.

But views of the Democratic Party have not drastically improved, with 41 percent reporting a positive view compared with 38 percent in 2024. Respondents had a net negative view of Democrats with negative sentiment jumping from 38 percent in 2024 to 42 percent last month.

Former Vice President Kamala Harris won the Latino vote by 3 percentage points in 2024, a drastic drop from former President Biden’s 25-point victory with the bloc in 2020. Trump won Latino men by 2 points in 2024 after Biden carried the group by 18 points four years earlier. A recent Cook Political Report survey found that 18 percent of Hispanic 2024 Trump voters disapproved of the job he’s doing.

The NBC News poll found that the surveyed Latino voters felt more motivated to vote compared with previous cycles. Fifty-four percent said they will vote to send a signal of opposition to Trump, and 65 percent of respondents said they feel Trump’s policies have hurt economic conditions. Sixty-seven percent said Trump’s immigration enforcement efforts have gone too far.

Inflation and the cost of living were ranked as the most important issues facing the country, followed by government corruption and threats to democracy. Respondents said they think Democrats would do a better job at protecting democracy, addressing the concerns of the Hispanic community, and handling immigration. The poll found the parties tied in respondents’ view of who would better protect the border.

The poll was conducted Sept. 21-28 by Hart Research Associates and Public Opinion Strategies and carries a margin of error of 3.46 points.

articles.title: What Hegseth needs is a new ‘Project Solarium’
articles.summary: What might be done to ensure Project Meridian succeeds?
articles.body:
Last week, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced six major defense initiatives that, if properly executed, could transform how the Department predicts and reacts to future battlefields.

The first two are the most relevant. The first is creation of a new four star Autonomous Warfare Command, which will build on and exploit Project Agincourt , assisted by the Defense Innovative Unit that will “overhaul the way the U.S. military buys, tests and uses drones and other cutting-edge weapons.”

The second, known as “ Project Meridian, ” which may prove to be the more imaginative. In Meridian, he has tasked billionaires Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey and former House Speaker Newt Gingrich (R-Ga.) to “ study the battlefields of the future, identify which weapons and technologies warfighters will need to harness to dominate in these environments, and propose actionable solutions to start developing, testing and fielding these capabilities no later than Jan. 28, or 120 days from now.”

Musk, with his hugely successful Starlink and Tesla companies, is the best known and is perhaps the 21st century combination of a Henry Ford and John D. Rockefeller. But Musk will be greatly handicapped by his role in heading the Department of Government Efficiency — that failed enterprise aimed at cutting government waste — given the powerful negative reactions it provoked from within the Pentagon.

Luckey , inventor of the Oculus visual reality headset, started Anduril in 2017. Anduril is a leading edge technology company focused on autonomous drones and sensors it is providing for the Department of Defense that are being used operationally in the war against Iran. Anduril just received a $20 billion non-compete contract with the Army.

Gingrich, elected to the House in 1978 and armed with a Ph.D. in European history, was well known for his efforts in leading military reform long before he became Speaker in 1995. In 1981, Gingrich co-founded the Caucuses on Military Reform and Space. His idea was to debate concepts and strategy rather than budget line items. Always controversial for his military deferments during the Vietnam War and for marrying his former high school teacher, Gingrich was a major force in bringing Republicans back to power.

Although this combination of minds is formidable on paper, none has been to war or commanded troops in action. It is therefore unclear that what Meridian will achieve that is feasible, technically possible and affordable. Indeed, some might argue that a Hollywood studio might be as creative. But, Hegseth has certainly generated interest.

So what might be done to ensure Meridian succeeds? As Gingrich knows, history offers a solution. When Dwight Eisenhower assumed the presidency in January 1953, he commissioned Project Solarium , an effort to determine national security strategy for dealing with the Soviet Union. Three separate task forces were empowered, each with a different set of assumptions. Hegseth should consider emulating this multi-task force organization.

Two additional groups should be established. One would consist of our most experienced past senior officers. The other would be formed under the vice chairman of the joint chiefs, with the four star geographic and functional combatant commanders.

Nominees for that second group should include former chairmen of the joint chiefs (as well as former service heads) Admiral Mike Mullen and Marine General Joseph Dunford ; Army General David Petraeus , with extraordinary experience in Afghanistan and Iraq; Air Force General Philip Breedlove , former supreme allied commander Europe; and Air Force General John Hyten , former commander strategic command and vice chairman, with an extensive background in space.

All three groups would initially operate independently.

In emulating Ike’s Solarium, Hegseth would bring together the best of the best regarding innovation, strategic thinking and current relevance, based on what the combatant commanders are doing today and in contemplating the future.

Some will be concerned that the Musk-Luckey-Gingrich team will produce ideas so over-the-top as to be unserious. Some may think that retired flag officers may be insufficiently informed to invalidate their findings. And still others might assume that combatant commanders are too wedded to the present — that considering the future is beyond their charter.

These doubters are wrong. Solarium as a model is perfect if we are to devise what national security needs. But will Hegseth agree?

Harlan Ullman is chairman of a private company, and principal author of the doctrine of shock and awe. His next book, co-written with Field Marshal The Lord David Richards, former U.K. chief of defense and due out this Fall, is “Who Thinks Best Wins: How Decisive Strategic Thinking Will Prevent Global Chaos .”

articles.summary: Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) said Sunday he would run for president in 2028 “if a bunch of goobers” seek the Republican nomination. During an appearance on NBC’s “Meet the Press,” the Louisiana Republican said his plans “right now” are to run for reelection to the Senate in 2028. But Kennedy noted that if he does…
articles.body:
Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) said Sunday he would run for president in 2028 “if a bunch of goobers” seek the Republican nomination .

During an appearance on NBC’s “Meet the Press,” the Louisiana Republican said his plans “right now” are to run for reelection to the Senate in 2028 .

But Kennedy noted that if he does not think he “can be effective” in the upper chamber, he “would consider” a bid for the Oval Office.

“I haven’t made a decision. … On my side of the aisle, if a bunch of goobers run, and I think they’re goobers, and one of the goobers might win, and I think I could do a better job, I would consider running. But right now, I’m running for reelection,” he told host Kristen Welker.

Kennedy, who entered the upper chamber in 2017, has campaigned for Senate Republicans in multiple states this year, including when he visited Nebraska to stump for Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-Neb.) last month.

Kennedy will be 77 on Jan. 20, 2029, the date of the next scheduled presidential inauguration.

If elected and sworn in as president that year, Kennedy would become the third-oldest president at the time of inauguration — behind President Trump at the start of his second term and former President Biden.

Vice President Vance leads in the majority of polls for the potential 2028 GOP field. A survey from Harvard University, the Harris Poll and HarrisX conducted in late September found Vance leading Donald Trump Jr. by 15 points among Republican respondents.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., former U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Nikki Haley and political commentator Tucker Carlson rounded out the top six.

The vice president told Robert Costa of CBS News in June he would discuss a presidential run with his wife, second lady Usha Vance, after the November midterms. Usha Vance gave birth to the couple’s fourth child in July.

When Welker asked John Kennedy about the possibility of running against the vice president, he shot her down, saying he was “not going to talk about” another potential 2028 candidate.

“I’m just not there yet,” the Louisiana Republican added. “I assume JD is going to run … but I think it’ll be good for both parties to … have a full field.”

articles.title: Appeals court pauses fired federal prosecutor’s reinstatement
articles.summary: An appeals court panel on Sunday paused a lower judge’s ruling that ordered the Trump administration to immediately reinstate Roger Rogoff as the top federal prosecutor in Seattle. President Trump ousted Rogoff in July from the U.S. attorney’s office in the Western District of Washington, less than an hour after he was sworn in following…
articles.body:
An appeals court panel on Sunday paused a lower judge’s ruling that ordered the Trump administration to immediately reinstate Roger Rogoff as the top federal prosecutor in Seattle.

President Trump ousted Rogoff in July from the U.S. attorney’s office in the Western District of Washington, less than an hour after he was sworn in following his unanimous appointment by federal judges.

U.S. District Judge Stanley Bastian, an appointee of former President Obama, sided with Rogoff’s claim that his termination was unlawful and ordered the Trump administration to restore him to the position until a successor is chosen through the Senate confirmation process.

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

The Trump administration quickly sought an emergency stay to halt the order while an appeal played out.

The 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals granted the administration’s request on Sunday, noting in an unsigned order that it was “only intended to preserve the status quo” as the case moves forward.

Rogoff’s lawyers noted in a filing Monday that while he “does not concede” that the administration is likely to prevail, he would remain out of the role for now.

The case stems from a dispute over who has the power to fire court-appointed U.S. attorneys, a question that has not yet been tested in federal court.

Rogoff has argued that Trump lacks the constitutional and statutory authority to unilaterally remove him. The Justice Department contends that the president can fire any U.S. attorney regardless of who appointed them.

Federal law states that the head of the Justice Department can appoint an interim replacement for up to 120 days when a vacancy arises for a U.S. attorney. Once that time is up, district court judges may appoint someone to “serve until the vacancy is filled,” which is how Rogoff came to lead the prosecutor’s office.

“Neither Congress nor the President can unilaterally and permanently fill the office,” Bastian wrote in his Oct. 1 order. “The two branches must work together to fill the office for longer than the short periods of time authorized by the statutes.”

Trump nominated Pete Serrano, who serves as the first assistant for the Eastern District of Washington, to fill the Seattle post last month.

articles.body:
It’s Monday. And your 12:30 Report authors ask that you please refrain from searching for us on Venmo.

Programming note : Hello! We are Elliott Davis and Steff Danielle Thomas filling in for Cate. Please send your tips, comments and story ideas to edavis@thehill.com or sthomas@thehill.com .

The Associated Press | J. Scott Applewhite

The Supreme Court’s new term is officially underway, after oral arguments began Monday morning in a major climate case that pits state and local governments against fossil fuel companies over the costs of climate change.

Boulder, Colo., sued ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy Inc. years ago, accusing the two energy giants of deceiving people over the harms of fossil fuels and costing the city money as a result.

Justice Samuel Alito recused himself from the case last week with no explanation. But the associate justice has otherwise spoken up in some rare media appearances in recent days.

On Sunday, Alito told Fox News that he tries not to pay too much attention to President Trump’s praise of him, and he added that he hopes his colleagues do the same when the shoe is on the other foot.

The president told Time magazine in an interview last week that he regrets nominating conservative Justices Amy Coney Barrett , Neil Gorsuch and Brett Kavanaugh , saying they vote against him “too often” in Supreme Court orders and rulings. Trump, however, frequently commends Alito, recently referring to him and Justice Clarence Thomas as “legends.”

The Supreme Court’s term is starting on shaky ground with Trump, as its docket has been filling up with cases that are key to the president’s agenda amid his criticisms of several justices, The Hill’s Zach Schonfeld and Sophie Brams report.

In the same “Fox News Sunday” interview, Alito said he has an “opinion” on who leaked the draft opinion of justices overturning Roe v. Wade in 2022, but he declined to elaborate. He also told CBS News last week that he considered retirement at the end of the court’s last term.

In other news tied to the high court Monday, the justices declined to take up cases about a school ban on shirts emblazoned with a slogan mocking former President Biden , an appeal from the convicted NXIVM sex cult leader and an attempt by the 2015 Charleston, S.C., church massacre shooter to disqualify his trial judge.

Apparently mum’s the word for Sen. Tom Cotton (R-Ark.), who has not directly addressed the fact that Trump posted the lawmaker’s cellphone number on Truth Social over the weekend as part of the president’s push for Congress to pass a bill making daylight saving time permanent.

Cotton has remained steadfast in his opposition to the legislation, due at least in part to its potential impact on Arkansans.

But if he has a problem with Trump putting him on blast, he hasn’t said so publicly yet. In response to a request for comment, Cotton’s office referred The Hill to the lawmaker’s broader statement on the bill.

A Venmo account linked to the number Trump posted was reportedly flooded with payment requests over the weekend. Reports also indicated that attempts to call the cell were met with a notice that the number had been disconnected.

Another GOP senator’s take: Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) addressed Trump posting Cotton’s cell number in an interview with NBC News’s “Meet the Press” on Sunday.

It would be a disservice to paraphrase the quote, so here you go: “The president, as we know, can be sometimes — he exists loudly. He can be tempestuous. He can go from zero to a‑‑hole in about three seconds.”

With both chambers of Congress on recess until after the midterm elections, lawmakers are hitting the campaign trail this week with just a month until Election Day.

In the latest edition of This Week on the Hill for Insiders, Sudiksha Kochi lays out the debates and campaign stops to watch for.

Trump and Vice President Vance have also spent weeks rallying voters in support of vulnerable Republican candidates. Today, they will continue the campaign blitz with events in Nebraska and Alaska.

The Trump administration is closely monitoring a possible case of pneumonic plague in Russia after a 28-year-old laboratory worker died from a mysterious illness.

All eyes on Siberia: The State Department told NewsNation, The Hill’s partner network, that it is working with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and other agencies to track the situation.

“We are aware of reports of a fatal case of suspected pneumonic plague in Irkutsk Oblast, Russia,” an official said, cautioning that many details remain unconfirmed.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio noted to reporters on Monday that while the administration is keeping tabs on the situation, it has not “caused an alarm.”

At the center: A young woman working at an institute in Siberia that researches plague and other infectious diseases. Russian authorities say she died from pneumonia of unknown origin and have not confirmed whether the plague was responsible.

Around 200 people are reportedly under medical observation, while Russia’s top health watchdog traveled to the region.

Particularly nasty strain: Pneumonic plague is the most serious form of the disease and can spread from person to person through infectious droplets, according to the CDC. Without treatment, it can be fatal, though the disease is treatable with commonly available antibiotics.

The catch: Russian officials say tests have not detected microorganisms associated with the woman’s work. Her cause of death remains unclear, and no broader outbreak has been confirmed.

Former White House COVID-19 response coordinator Dr. Deborah Birx called the researcher’s death “particularly concerning,” raising the possibility that a lab accident could be behind the case.

Birx also pointed to reports that the woman traveled after a possible exposure, warning she “potentially could have exposed many people” because pneumonic plague can spread through respiratory droplets.

“So, a lot of concerns and a lot of reasons for the Russians to be transparent,” the doctor added.

articles.title: Teach our sons that the only cause of rape is a rapist
articles.summary: Marine veteran Joslin Joseph argues against the prevalence of victim-blaming culture following the Cornell rape investigation, asserting that accountability must lie solely with perpetrators.
articles.body:
When I was in the Marines, one of my fellow Marines came to me with a problem. She had been hanging out at the barracks with several people from our unit. She got drunk, ended up dancing with a guy who was a higher rank, and went up to her room. She said what happened next was not consensual. The guy she was talking about was my best friend at the time. I did what I thought was the right thing.

I reported it to our Gunnery Sergeant and our unit’s leadership started looking into it. She later dropped the complaint because she was told that if she pursued it, she would also get into trouble for underage drinking, having alcohol in the barracks, and fraternization. Now, hearing her story, I was convinced that my friend had done wrong, but when I bought it up I was told. “It is he said/she said. And she never should have put herself in that position.”

When I was in college at Ohio State, I went to a Halloween house party. A girl showed up with a costume that was way too revealing, drawing jealousy from the ladies and lots of attention from the guys. As the night and drinking went on, guys started getting too forward with her. She eventually put on a coat but a guy ripped it off and groped her. He was kicked out and she was crying. As I left the party later, my girlfriend at the time remarked, “Well what did she expect showing up like that?”

The fallout from the Cornell rape story hasn’t even settled yet and we are once again struggling with the notion that women have to be perfect in order to not be raped. The onus should not be on women. Instead, we need to teach men that there is one rule when it comes to rape.

Look, the Cornell controversy isn’t limited to the school and already has turned political . And everyone is trying to talk about the nuances of the case while trying not to be attacked for “victim blaming” or being part of a lynch mob. Sunny Hostin of “The View” came under attack for talking about the legal tripwire that comes with charging men with rape when there is contradictory evidence. Trump has declared the Cornell 7, as they are called, won’t get a fair shake because the investigator into the case also successfully prosecuted him.

There is going to be a lot of talk again about what consent actually is, when does “no” mean no, and why the system always seems to fail. Now, I know as much as you do at this point, but it can be fair to assume that the university didn’t do nearly enough to look into the matter. For that matter, neither did the district attorney. This isn’t a new phenomenon.

When I worked at Baylor University in corporate partnerships, a huge scandal rocked the school over the university working to cover up instances of rape by members of the football team. I would meet with donors, local sponsors and alumni and the conversation always drifted toward the scandal. And it always veered toward victim blaming or conspiracies. (Evidently, it was all a smear campaign by a very jealous University of Texas according to some people in Waco).

Between that and the first two instances I talked about, there was always the same pattern. A lack of accountability from the men. We live in an era where people are freaking about masculinity in this country (or a lack thereof). Some in the manosphere have taken a stance that women need protecting. We can’t have trans women playing sports because we need to protect the women. But somehow, we can’t work to hold ourselves accountable from protecting women from rape by men.

It doesn’t matter if you are a man who claims to be a feminist or a so-called alpha male in the manosphere. The change in attitude that should have been adopted during MeToo should have come from us. The only cause of rape is when men make the choice. The choice to ignore a no. The choice to take advantage when you know better. The choice to walk away. The choice to accept it won’t be your night to get lucky.

It’s also the choice to speak up. Several of the men in this case claimed they were very uncomfortable. Well, it shouldn’t take an Ivy League education to realize when you are in a situation that is clearly uncomfortable, you probably need to speak up. Apologizing after the fact , as one of the accused did, or claiming that you were the victim too as another did is not the answer.

We are nowhere near close to knowing what actually happened that night. Despite living in a world where a digital trail makes evidence more easily obtainable, this still might end up a case that is she said/they said. But we can finally start doing the right thing and teaching young men and boys this situation. And teach that the only cause of rape is a rapist and that is an easy choice to make in any situation.

Joslin Joseph is a recipient of the Military Reporters and Editors award for Best Commentary /Opinion. A graduate of Harvard and Ohio State, he is a Marine veteran who served in Iraq. He currently lives in Anaheim, Calif.

articles.body:
Former President Obama is set to rally later this month in Michigan for Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed, who’s in a must-win battleground race against Republican Mike Rogers.

“It is my honor and privilege to announce that President @BarackObama is joining us on the trail in Detroit on Saturday, October 24,” El-Sayed announced on the social platform X .

Obama’s visit will kick off the first day of in-person early voting in the Great Lakes State, as the former president gets more involved in the midterms. He will also campaign alongside Democratic gubernatorial candidate Jocelyn Benson.

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

The former president campaigned in Texas with Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico earlier this year, and he appeared in a campaign ad with Iowa Senate candidate Josh Turek this summer. The Associated Press reported that more Obama campaign stops are to be announced.

Former Vice President Kamala Harris was also in Michigan last month to boost El-Sayed, stressing the stakes of the seat for Democrats on key issues.

El-Sayed, a doctor and former head of health departments in Detroit and Wayne County, faces President Trump-endorsed Rogers, a former congressman, in a race that Cook Political Report considers a toss-up and Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ) puts under the “lean” Democratic label.

Rogers narrowly lost the 2024 Senate election to Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.), as Trump flipped the state and defeated Harris, and he is now vying for retiring Sen. Gary Peters’s (D-Mich.) seat.

Winning the seat could be pivotal to Democrats’ hopes of flipping the Senate, where they need to net four seats to take control. DDHQ now forecasts that Democrats have a narrow, 56 percent probability of winning the upper chamber, compared with a 76 percent chance of winning the House.

Jon Husted (R) in Youngstown next week, marking his second trip to the Buckeye State in a month as the incumbent faces an uphill climb. The Oct. 12 rally comes as several polls show Husted trailing former Sen. Sherrod Brown (D-Ohio). A New York Times/Siena College poll…
articles.body:
President Trump will campaign with incumbent Ohio Sen. Jon Husted (R) in Youngstown next week, marking his second trip to the Buckeye State in a month as the incumbent faces an uphill climb.

The Oct. 12 rally comes as several polls show Husted trailing former Sen. Sherrod Brown (D-Ohio). A New York Times/Siena College poll released Saturday showed Brown leading Husted 49 percent to 46 percent among likely voters, a lead that was well inside the poll’s 4.5 percent margin of error.

The same survey showed Trump’s approval rating in the state at 38 percent, while his disapproval was at 60 percent.

Trump hit the campaign trail with Husted on Saturday, stumping in the Dayton suburb of Vandalia. The Hill was the first national outlet to report on the Oct. 12 rally.

Other recent polls also have shown Brown with a narrow lead. A Suffolk University poll released late last month showed the former senator leading Husted 47 percent to 44 percent among registered voters, while a Marist poll released around the same time showed Brown leading 51 percent to 43 percent among registered voters.

Trump carried the state in the 2016, 2020, and 2024 presidential elections. He won the state in 2024 by just more than 11 percentage points.

Husted, who previously served as lieutenant governor, was appointed to fill Vice President Vance’s Senate seat in Ohio last year. Brown, who was first elected to the Senate in 2006, lost his reelection bid to Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) in 2024.

Data centers have become a flashpoint in the Ohio Senate contest, with Trump touting the facilities on the trail.

“We want them,” Trump said, referring to data centers during Saturday’s rally in Vandalia. “Look, there’s so much money to be made for Ohio, you can’t just turn them off. They’ll go to China.”

articles.title: Vance argues pro-Trump campaign ads ‘are not partisan’
articles.summary: Vice President Vance said the new pro-President Trump television advertisements are “not partisan” amid criticism from both sides of the aisle. The ads, which cost $20 million of taxpayer money, feature Trump’s voice calling for the defeat of socialism and communism while touting the “largest tax cuts in history” and “reigniting American manufacturing.” The Trump…
articles.body:
Vice President Vance said the new pro-President Trump television advertisements are “not partisan” amid criticism from both sides of the aisle.

The ads, which cost $20 million of taxpayer money , feature Trump’s voice calling for the defeat of socialism and communism while touting the “largest tax cuts in history” and “reigniting American manufacturing.”

The Trump administration has claimed the ads are public service announcements, not campaign ads.

Vance said there is a history of the federal government using tax dollars to advertise the government’s recent actions, pointing specifically to the Obama administration’s ads on the Affordable Care Act. Trump halted that advertising effort at the start of his first term.

“Living in a constitutional republic, you have to be honest with the American people about what you’re doing, about what’s going on and part of that is getting out there and telling the message,” Vance said, adding that the ads are not partisan but rather are about “how great” the country is.

Defeating communism in America has become a key message for Republicans as they try to retain control of Congress in the November midterms.

Trump has also said the ads are fair game, claiming they do not outwardly support him or a particular candidate. He said the ads are for the “spirit of the country” and that while he would gladly personally pay for them, he believes there is no issue.

The ads prominently feature the president’s image and voice and have been aired during NFL games and on Fox News, CNN and MS NOW.

Opponents of the president have labeled the ads as illegal.

Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.) said the ads violate the Hatch Act, a law that limits political activities among government employees and restricts government resources from being used for political purposes. GOP Sen. Thom Tillis (N.C.) said the ads are “inappropriate” and compared them to something former right-wing Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán would do.

Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chair Brendan Carr said the ads are “ normal public service announcements ” that do not merit any FCC review.

articles.title: Democrats add 6 more House races to ‘Red to Blue’ seat flipping list
articles.summary: The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) announced Monday it is adding six candidates to its list of potential flips. The DCCC added the candidates to its “Red to Blue” program, less than a month before the midterm elections. Via their inclusion on the list — which now includes 46 Democrats seeking to flip GOP-favored seats…
articles.body:
The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) announced Monday it is adding six candidates to its list of potential flips .

The DCCC added the candidates to its “Red to Blue” program, less than a month before the midterm elections .

Via their inclusion on the list — which now includes 46 Democrats seeking to flip GOP-favored seats — the candidates will receive “organizational and fundraising support,” along with strategic guidance, staff resources and training, the DCCC noted in a release .

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

The six candidates now on the “Red to Blue” list include Chris Jones, Dwayne Romero and Eliott Rodriguez, who are challenging GOP Reps. French Hill (Ark.), Jeff Hurd (Colo.) and María Elvira Salazar (Fla.), respectively.

Also on the list are Teresa Benitez-Thompson, Blake Gendebien and Justin Pearson, facing off against Nevada Republican David Flippo, New York Republican Anthony Constantino and Tennessee state Sen. Brent Taylor (R), respectively.

In 2024, President Trump won the six districts the DCCC has highlighted by an average of roughly 16 points.

Rep. Suzan DelBene (D-Wash.), the chair of the DCCC, argued the six Democratic candidates are “winning over voters with their message of lowering costs,” as inflation remains above 3 percent amid the Iran war, which has stretched into its seventh month.

“At a time when so many families are struggling to pay the bills, Americans deserve representatives who will actually fight to make their lives better,” DelBene added in the committee’s release. “Less than one month out from Election Day, voters are ready to turn the page on House Republicans’ broken promises and elect Democrats to the House Majority.”

Democrats need to flip a net of three seats in November to capture a 218-217 majority in the lower chamber. As of Monday, Decision Desk HQ gives Democrats a 76 percent chance to win back the House.

Brooke Butler, the political director of the DCCC, said Sunday she believes Democrats could capture up to 240 House seats next month.

“Anywhere between 218 and 240 feels very viable,” she told Politico . “We feel confident that we will get to 218. The question that I’ve told people from the beginning cycle is, ‘How much?’”

Mike Marinella, a spokesperson for the National Republican Congressional Committee, told The Hill the DCCC “is stretching its map a mile wide and an inch deep, pretending every district in America is suddenly a battleground.”

Marinella added, “Democrats can put as many names on a list as they want, but they’re still begging for resources just to match Republicans’ air superiority while bailing out their radical socialist nominees.”

images.caption: Rep. Suzan DelBene (D-Wash.) and The Hill’s senior political correspondent Amie Parnes discuss the Democrats’ midterm strategy during the second annual Hill Nation Summit at the Hamilton Hotel in Washington, D.C., on July 15, 2026.

articles.title: Jack Smith seen sporting ‘No Kings’ T-shirt at Power to the People festival
articles.summary: Jack Smith is apparently swapping the suit and tie he wears when testifying at the Capitol for a “No Kings” T-shirt. The former special counsel was eyed over the weekend sporting a tee from a Bruce Springsteen concert tour bearing the pointed message while attending a music festival featuring some of President Trump’s most vocal…
articles.body:
Jack Smith is apparently swapping the suit and tie he wears when testifying at the Capitol for a “No Kings” T-shirt. The former special counsel was eyed over the weekend sporting a tee from a Bruce Springsteen concert tour bearing the pointed message while attending a music festival featuring some of President Trump’s most vocal high-profile critics.

Smith was one of thousands of attendees at Saturday’s Power to the People festival in Columbia, Md., according to multiple photos and videos of the event posted on social media. In some images, Smith — wearing a black T-shirt from Springsteen’s Land of Hope and Dreams tour with the “No Kings” text at the bottom — was seen clutching a drink as he moved through the crowd. Other photographs show him smiling while posing with concertgoers.

In May, Springsteen announced he would perform at the one-day Power to the People gathering, along with the Foo Fighters, Tom Morello, Dave Matthews, Joan Baez and other artists.

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

The festival, “curated by Morello,” was billed by organizers as a way to bring together “artists, fans, activists, organizations and community leaders for an unforgettable day celebrating the power of music and collective action to inspire change.”

The shirt that Smith was seen wearing promoted Springsteen’s nationwide Land of Hope and Dreams tour earlier this year. The 77-year-old “Born in the U.S.A.” singer had said he was launching the tour “in defense of America,” telling fans in a February video that the country’s ideals are “under attack” by Trump and his “rogue government.”

At the Power to the People concert, Foo Fighters’ frontman Dave Grohl reportedly appeared to give a shoutout to the former special counsel in the crowd, dedicating the band’s song “My Hero” to “my new friend Jack.”

Grohl also seemingly offered a sartorial nod to Smith by wearing an Iowa Hawkeyes shirt onstage during his performance. The shirt appeared to be a reference to Sen. Eric Schmitt’s (R-Mo.) line of questioning of Smith during a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing last week. During the hearing, Schmitt erroneously accused the prosecutor of attending an Atlanta Hawks game — rather than an Iowa Hawkeyes game — in an effort to tie Smith to a Georgia prosecution of Trump.

articles.title: White House blocks Politico from Air Force One
articles.summary: The White House on Monday will prohibit Politico from boarding Air Force One and fulfilling its pool duties covering President Trump.
